# TTS (TEXT TO SPEECH) USING MINIMAX H3

## 14th November 2026 (version 7 of workflow)

- I removed the speedup loras and set the steps to 25 then 30. It didnt fix the metallic issues (some even say 50 but I didnt see improvements there either). 15 seconds of video took about 4 minutes on my 3060 RTX. </br>

- If you get garble, try reducing the clip length. This is about packing the words in without pauses in the main delivery, then cutting them up later for edit into better timing in post. But watch it doesnt speed the words up too much.

nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
# Mark DK Berry 

YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry)

Patreon: [https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies](https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies)

Workflows: [https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows)

---

## Latent Space Upscaler workflow

**Useage**: I made this specifically for dialogue clip upscaling as my other one doesnt work for mouth movements. This does.


NOTE: I prefer results from my pixel space upscaling workflow which is _"MBEDIT - MH3_r2v_SingleSampler_Detailer_vXX.json"_ and you can download it from here [https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows/tree/main/workflows_by_model/Minimax-H3](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows/tree/main/workflows_by_model/Minimax-H3)

but unfortunately that one doesnt do a good job with dialogue clips and fights mouth movements, even with good prompting. 

So, I created this workflow specifically for dialogue clips.

---

## ISSUES/THINGS TO BE AWARE OF

- **OOMS will hit you in the 2nd sampler, and are a PITA after waiting 20 mins to find out it cant handle it**. But if you have dynamic memory in, no switches, and dont dump the models during the wf, you should be able to tweak the Latent Upscaler down a touch and get through the 2nd sampler without a restart, so long as you dont change setting further back. Then tweak it better for next go.</br>

- I would prefer to set `ref_image_size` in the main H3 node of first part of run, to "Max" but often have to go with "Match" instead to avoid OOMs and get higher resolution faster.



---

## Upscaler Model For This Workflow 

You could install whatever ones you think are best. I tried some others but didnt find them to be as good as this one. This one still needed tweaking to get right, and might need different settings for your rig.

- [https://github.com/LBH-123-AI/Comfyui_Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler](https://github.com/LBH-123-AI/Comfyui_Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler)

- [https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler)

---

## USING THIS WORKFLOW

It's not a v2v workflow like the pixel space upscaler _(see top of this note for that)_. This was created for upscaling dialogue clips.

***The following is for my 3060 RTX 12GB VRAM, 32 GB System ram as a guide for what to expect. Season to your tastes and setup.***

1. Set "H3 Reference to Video" node to resolution of 0.4 mp or higher if you can handle it. (for my dialogue clips I need at least 8 seconds, so its my limit vrs time)

2. Make a good prompt using the minimax prompt guide and an LLM, and provide your ref images for characters and scene.

3. Set the chunks to manage VRAM ceiling vrs Time. Set your speed Loras and speedups as required. (They change all the time so see other notes above).

4. set the Latent Upscaling node (LBH-123-AI notes will help you set it up) to whatever wont oom at your video clip length, longer it will take and more likely to OOM. I leave it at 0.8mp now as I stay under the oom for 15 and 20 seconds long clips at that.

# PROMPT DEVELOPMENT:


This is for MMH3 TTS audio voice only. its fast and dirty way to get Voice Overs. A 15 second audio clip is completed in under 100 seconds on a 3060 RTX.

NOTE: the most common issue for garbled dialogue is too many words and not enough time. 15 seconds will get two average lines of dialogue (30 words total). reduce words is best first test if you get continual problems. Increase to max of 20 seconds if you really need to try to get it in.

## APPROACH

- all images are disabled and the size is set to 32 x 32 pixels. (add them in if it helps target speakers) 
- one audio file is provided for voice cloning, set to 30 seconds lenght max.
- output length is 15 seconds, as per usual. 
- disable VEDA as it does cause audio issues and wont add a hit here.
- to keep consistency of audio results (eq, tone, timbre) I keep the same speed-up loras and settings in that I use in main runs.

## FOR TTS START HERE AND TWEAK UNTIL IT WORKS FOR YOU

```
subject_definitions:
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for the off-screen narrator (S1), containing a spoken English vocal layer.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] The target video is a static shot of a plain dark wall while an off-screen narrator (S1) delivers a voiceover, with the voice timbre following <Audio 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - the narrator's voice timbre and measured delivery follow <Audio 1> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
The target video is a minimal live-action shot of a dimly lit plain wall with no people on screen.
[Shot 1] The camera holds a static shot of the plain wall. The off-screen narrator (S1), in the voice timbre referenced from <Audio 1> at a calm, measured pace, says in an off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] YOUR SCRIPT LINE HERE.</d>

overall_soundscape:
N/A

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
```

## THIS WORKED BETTER FOR ME

```
subject_definitions:
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for the narrator (S1), containing a spoken English vocal layer.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] The target video is a static shot of a plain dark wall while a narrator (S1) delivers a voiceover, with the voice timbre following <Audio 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - the narrator's voice timbre and measured delivery follow <Audio 1> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
The target video is a minimal live-action shot of a dimly lit plain wall with no people on screen.
[Shot 1] The camera holds a static shot of the plain wall. The narrator (S1), in the voice timbre referenced from <Audio 1> says, <d>[English] healthy masculinity is resisting the emotional pressure to shut down, close off, or conform to rigid expectations.</d>

overall_soundscape:
The sterile room hums with the soft whir of computer fans.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
```

## FOR TWO SPEAKERS (2 AUDIO FILES)

```
subject_definitions:
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for the narrator (S1), containing a spoken English vocal layer.
<Audio 2> is the voice-timbre reference for the narrator (S2), containing a spoken English vocal layer.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] The target video is a static shot of a plain dark wall while two off-screen speakers (S1 and S2) exchange lines in voiceover, with S1's timbre following <Audio 1> and S2's timbre following <Audio 2>.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - the narrator's voice timbre and measured delivery follow <Audio 1> without copying the original signal.
<Audio 2>: reference - the second speaker's voice timbre and delivery follow <Audio 2> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
The target video is a minimal live-action shot of a dimly lit plain wall with no people on screen.

[Shot 1] The camera holds a static shot of the plain wall. The narrator (S1), in the voice timbre referenced from <Audio 1> in a female Canadian voice says, <d>[English] Healthy masculinity is resisting the emotional pressure to shut down, close off, or conform to rigid expectations.</d>

After a short pause, the second off-screen speaker (S2), in the voice timbre referenced from <Audio 2> in a London cockney accent says, <d>[English] Fine when you live in entitled modern luxury, but a man must be able to kill dinner when the pressure is on.</d>

overall_soundscape:
The sterile room hums with the soft whir of computer fans.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

```

## THIS ALSO WORKED WELL TWO SPEAKERS, TWO REF IMAGES, TWO AUDIO FILES

```
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the young man from <Picture 1>
<Subject 2> is the man from <Picture 2>
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 1> (S1), containing a spoken English vocal layer.
<Audio 2> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 2> (S2), containing a spoken English vocal layer.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] The target video is a static shot while two speakers (S1 and S2) exchange lines, with S1's timbre following <Audio 1> and S2's timbre following <Audio 2>.

detailed_description:

[shot 1 ] close up on <subject 1> from <picture 1>

<Subject 1> (S1), speaking in the female Canadian voice timbre referenced from <Audio 1> says, <d>[English] Healthy masculinity involves allowing yourself to be expressive. Such as smiling or talking with your hands, instead of suppressing those behaviors.</d>

[shot 2] camera turns to <subject 2> from <picture 2>

<Subject 2> (S2), speaking in a London cockney voice timbre referenced from <Audio 2> says, <d>[English] And how did those qualities help when you were held captive by an ape?</d>

overall_soundscape:
The sterile room hums with the soft whir of computer fans.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
```
